newsitem.title: USA: US Airways attendants get award over S.C. crash.
newsitem.headline: US Airways attendants get award over S.C. crash.

text.p: A South Carolina judge has awarded one flight attendant close to $1 million and another $570,000 in damages in connection with the 1994 crash of USAir Flight 1016 near Charlotte, North Carolina in which they suffered burns.

An assistant to U.S. District Judge Joe Anderson said the judge awarded nearly $1 million in damages to Karen Forcht and almost $570,000 to Richard Demary in an order issued on Tuesday, the result of a bench hearing in December.

The two flight attendants sued the U.S. government, saying they suffered both emotional and physical injury in the accident. The U.S. government has conceded that its air traffic controllers were partly to blame for the crash, and workers' compensation laws prevented the attendants from suing the airline.
Demary was hailed as a hero for helping many passengers escape from the plane. Forcht, although more severely burned than Demary in the accident, helped Demary move passengers away from the wreckage.
In his ruling, Anderson wrote that the two attendants' injuries were exacerbated because of their jobs.

"This is because of their special feelings of responsibility to protect their passengers, and the associate guilt for failing to do so, even though there was, in reality, nothing further either of them could have done," he said.

The attendants' damages were the first of the crash awards to be made public. At least eight passengers and families of people killed settled with US Airways last month after a federal jury found the company at least partly at fault in the crash, but those amounts have been kept secret.
The DC-9 crashed in a violent thunderstorm on July 2, 1994, killing 37 people on board.
